newsitem.title: FINLAND: RESEARCH ALERT - SALOMON STARTS NOKIA AS "BUY".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - SALOMON STARTS NOKIA AS "BUY".

text.p: U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers said in a report dated June 6 it initiated coverage of Finnish telecommuncations group Nokia as a "buy" and forecast the group's 1997 earnings per share at 16.2 markka versus 10.7.
It said Nokia was "still the cheapest stock in its peer group" trading at "what we consider to be an uwarranted discount to its peers" and set a one-year price target of 400 markka.
The report was based on a price of 346 markka. Nokia on Tuesday traded at 350.00 markka, down 4.00.
It said Nokia traded at 15-30 percent discounts to Swedish rival Ericsson, measured in price to earnings ratios.
"Through 1998, we expect Nokia to achieve compound annual sales growth surpassing 30 percent," Salomon said. "This is by far the highest projected sales growth in its peer group."
"In this period we anticipate Nokia having 12 percent operating margins versus nine percent or less for the other companies," the bank said.
"The company should be a major beneficiary of the convergence of wireless and fixed, data and voice communications," it said.
